title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents using gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this degenerate confirmatory outcome is a direct consequence of identical generated candidates producing no baseline execution faults. We report preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting (planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, model_calls_used = 72, artifact_count = 510), representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded recommendations for designs that can detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent→configuration translators for network operations. The promise is faster, higher-level change specification; the risk is executing generated device-level text that violates reachability, policy, ordering, or workflow invariants. A widely suggested operational guard is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture: stochastic LLM generation followed by deterministic verification and optional repair or human review. Despite architectural proposals and prototypes, there are few preregistered experiments that measure whether canonical deterministic verifiers actually detect and thereby prevent emulator-observed operational faults for identical LLM outputs. This paper answers a narrowly scoped, preregistered research question under controlled shared_initial_candidate semantics: does inserting a deterministic verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of generated configurations that would execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? The design intentionally isolates detection (verifier flagging) from benefits achievable via resampling, prompt engineering, or repair-enabled iterations. Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded, fully archived confirmatory run (72 paired intents) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 that yielded a ceiling/null result (zero baseline emulator faults). We analyze why that outcome follows from the preregistered contract, report exact numbers and diagnostics from archived traces, and provide concrete, artifact-supported recommendations for future preregistered designs able to detect verifier utility.
sections.related_work: Empirical and architectural work has explored LLM-driven intent→configuration translation, multi-agent tool-augmented NetOps, and generate–verify–repair ideas. Nguyen et al. report intent→configuration pipelines in constrained vendor-dialect emulator settings [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks propose integrated validation to reduce regressions [2]; GVR architectures have been studied in code and software domains where deterministic checkers and test suites validate stochastic outputs and drive repair [3]. Constraint-enforcing decoding and integer-programming constrained decoding reduce structured-output violations in other domains [4], suggesting complementary strategies for network outputs. Classical deterministic network-verification methods (header-space, policy-checkers) provide precise invariants but, to our knowledge, direct preregistered paired experiments that couple LLM generation with canonical verifiers and report emulator-observed outcomes on identical candidates are scarce [5]. Our work situates itself at the intersection of these threads by testing detector efficacy under a strict shared-initial-candidate confirmatory contract and by archiving all execution and analysis artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 and froze design and analysis before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis (H1) targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two-sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; power calculations gave ≈63 pairs needed and we preregistered N = 72 pairs (24 per topology-difficulty stratum) to allow margin for exclusions.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. The execution contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated in two conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record emulator fault/no-fault. Guarded: run the verifier on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no execution); if it does not flag, execute the same candidate and record emulator outcome. Because only a single shared candidate exists per intent the guarded arm cannot improve outcomes via resampling; any paired difference can only arise if the verifier flags a candidate that otherwise would have executed with a fault.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (provider = openai_responses, max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The configuration records temperature = null (provider-default runtime sampling semantics) and is archived. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0"), implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule set that yields a binary per-episode validity verdict plus structured validator_traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after final_state, violation_codes, difficulty metadata). All verifier traces were archived per episode.

Task-bank construction, contamination controls, and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task-manifest entry encodes a natural-language intent, a structured required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, initial and expected final states, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard). The preregistration mandated deterministic exact-match contamination checks using public corpora with exclusion rules: exact-match contamination => exclusion from confirmatory analysis. analysis/contamination_summary.csv records zero exact-match exclusions for the confirmatory set. The confirmatory sample remained stratified as preregistered: 24 pairs per stratum (medium/hard/very_hard).

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retries for transient hosted-API errors (3 attempts total) for generation calls; execution metadata logs all retries and provider-call events. The run wall-clock started at 2026-08-31T06:56:23.065707Z and completed at 2026-08-31T07:06:28.665518Z (≈10.1 minutes). The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72 (one shared generation per pair). Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, cache_miss_count = 72, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}. Artifact_count = 510 and representative artifact hashes for key files are archived in the manifest.
sections.results:
Execution and manifest summary. The pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary.csv records baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and exact inference. Aggregating across the 72 confirmatory pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) is [0.0, 0.0], reflecting the degenerate distribution produced by the absence of discordant pairs. analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain these tabulations and are archived.

Representative per-episode validator diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_trace fields with parsed_command_count between 2 and 6, required_command_count equal to parsed counts for valid sequences, validator_version = "5.0", score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", and violation_count = 0. Example (task-000001): required_sequence = [admin down edge1; mtu 1600 edge1; vlan 30 edge1; admin up edge1]; shared_initial_candidate normalized_configuration = "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600\ninterface edge1 admin up"; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true. These per-episode traces confirm the verifier executed and produced no flagging on all shared candidates.

Contamination, missingness, and sensitivity diagnostics. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed and archived; because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred these sensitivity analyses reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion (paired difference = 0.0). All analysis artifacts, including analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/condition_summary.csv, are archived and hashed.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation and causes. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment isolates verifier detection on identical generated candidates. Observing zero baseline faults leads to a ceiling/null confirmatory outcome: when the generator (gpt-5-mini) produced valid candidates for the preregistered synthetic corpus, the verifier had no executed faults to prevent. Archived, measurable factors that contributed to the ceiling outcome include: (1) the deterministic task generator produced highly constrained, explicit intents with structured required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields encoded in the task manifest (increasing unambiguousness); (2) gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json) generated candidates that matched those structured constraints across the corpus; and (3) the verifier rule set (full_intent_constraint_validation in deterministic_netops_validator_v5) aligns closely with required_sequence constraints, producing high congruence between generation objective and verifier checks. The artifacts substantiate each point (task-manifest payloads, normalized_configuration fields, validator_trace records).

Methodological implications and recommendations. A strict shared_initial_candidate confirmatory contract provides a clear detection test but by design cannot capture improvements that arise from verifier-triggered repairs or alternative generator samples. To measure practical verifier benefits in future preregistered runs we recommend artifact-grounded design modifications: (A) independent-generation arms that permit different initial samples per condition (so verifier-mediated resampling or repair can affect executed distributions); (B) repair-enabled flows allowing one deterministic repair call when the verifier flags violations and executing repaired candidates; (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks that inject ambiguity or protocol edge cases to raise baseline error prevalence; (D) multi-model and explicit sampling-parameter sweeps (set temperature explicitly) to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity. All proposed alternatives are compatible with the existing adapter/execution infrastructure and can be preregistered with the same deterministic tracing and artifact conventions.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates detection but prevents verifier-mediated candidate selection from influencing outcomes. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but do not capture timing- or traffic-dependent failure modes present in production hardware. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic/emulated task bank, and one deterministic verifier; extrapolation to other models, vendor dialects, or production devices is limited. Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero the confirmatory design had no statistical power to demonstrate verifier benefit here. Residual uncertainty: exact-match contamination checks found no inclusions, but private model training data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains a residual uncertainty documented in the manifest.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults; therefore the verifier could not reduce executed faults (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: if identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot improve outcomes under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires preregistered contracts that permit independent generation per arm, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model sampling sweeps. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced here are archived to enable reproducible follow-up experiments that implement those alternatives.

limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
